reviews.text: 这游戏跟astrea是什么关系？ 都是抛骰子爬塔 开始游戏的跳过都会被steam右下角弹出来的东西挡住 事件和商店设计都极为简陋 最最逆天的是，首发的机翻都烂到你经常看不懂卡牌含义的程度 等机翻改了再改好评 //2天后更新：它居然把跳过放到左下角去了！动作真快吧，我哭死 //正式版更新： 机翻还是逆天，各种错翻漏翻与非人类语序，这差评估计是改不掉了 顺便提一句游戏性上的问题，这游戏关键词设计真的过于多了，有些技能甚至有五六个关键词同时出现，一来对新手极度不友好，二来过多的体系大大增加了单个体系成型的难度。再加上破烂的平衡性，很多时候玩着玩着就忍不住想重开了

玩了几把，说实话，还是有点恶心人，这游戏负面的东西太折磨人了，还有这么多尬吹的吗？真就喜欢折磨人是吧？ 首先毒不吃护盾？那张roll骰子然后中毒的卡，升级后one turn叠四个毒，叠起来了把自己毒死了。。。真的牛马了 其次，我不懂你设计回血 +10 和 +25 这些意义何在？你不能让我回满吗？那我加血上限的收益在哪里？？？更别说就+8血上限一次，我还不如去打怪呢。 有的event，我拿个钱都要吃你一个永久负面的效果，作者你没病吧？？？ 三个物品格子，我用还是不用？效果不是特别强，用了感觉像鸡肋，不用很容易满了提示我要丢旧的才能拿新的，设计背包那么难吗？或者要不你改成装备吧，整点正面的装备效果都比这玩意强。 spell卡的平衡性太差，你绿卡、蓝卡、紫卡的强度区分呢？有些卡真的看着就鸡肋，还带负面效果，卡升级只能二选一但又不是特别强真的蠢，我求你抄一下其他游戏吧，要么更多的选择，要么你可以升两次或者更多次。否则，你这个就等于每张卡固定两个高级版本，也没多少自由度。 这个游戏负面东西那么多的情况下，玩家的提升却没有让人感到爽，暂时不推荐了。
可以玩，但是不够爽。 我就搞不明白打完boss了还不能回满血是个什么鬼，抠抠搜搜的，生怕玩家过关太轻松是吧。 还有那么多b解锁，哪来那么多需要解锁的东西。 然后稀有就蓝牌和绿牌，紫色呢金色呢？？是我需要往后解锁吗？打完boss给张传说牌不是约定俗成的了吗，就显得你特立独行呗，用脑子和爽就不能同时有是吗？

This is the sort of game an AI chatbot would tell you to make if you asked it about "a game like Slay the Spire, but maybe add some dice in there?". # Fixed - No 21:9 support. -> Fixed in a post-release patch - Some textures are too low-res for the size they're displayed at. The animation at the end of the fight looks ridiculous. -> Fixed in a post-release patch # Bad - Generally way too reliant on mimicking Slay the Spire. The map is topologically a carbon copy. The nodes are also the same. There's also "Elites". There's a "Shop". The hexagonal grid is there because they've heard hexagons are cool or something. - You collect yellow coins that you use in the shop. There's exactly three potion slots, and they're again called potions. After killing a boss, you choose one the special three special artifacts with a positive and negative effect. At least they're not relics, I guess. Someone was very persistent in the team to change at least one name. - The environment are bland, just like the enemies. The colors are all washed out; it's nothing like the game thumbnail. There's 0 charm in it. It looks like a mobile game. - Animations are blocking casting new spells, which often leads to your dragging not working, without any visual or auditive feedback, which leaves you confused and you have to check what dice you have left now, and if the spell was cast successfully or not. And then the game wants you to speed run it for an achievement. # Good - Some of the status effects affect the way enemies look. For example, an enemy with "Thorns" will be surrounded by actual thorns. - I love the QoL feature where hovering the "End Turn" button will show you the outcome of the turn. You can tell at a glance if you're good to go without calculating all minor numbers. There's nothing particularly terrible in it that will stop you from playing, but there's no reason to recommend this over the game it [strike]draws inspiration from[/strike] [strike]borrows from[/strike] just copies everything from. If you're gonna make another version of a genre-defining game, you have to make it either better or different enough. The core difference is just taken from Dicey Dungeon instead, which is an example of a "different enough" game you could also play instead of this mediocre knock-off. TL;DR: A carbon copy of Slay the Spire, but without any charm and worse on the technical side of things. Recommended only if you've 100%'d Slay the Spire and Dicey Dungeons and for some reason you want to start all over again, but this time you want to look at unimaginative 3D environments and listen to elevator music.

I like "Roguelite" games and had fun with this exploring the mechanics and getting a handle of what was needed for success, but quickly found that my interest waned due to balancing and the repetitive nature of the game after a while. The aren't a large number of paths to victory, so you keep looking to acquire the same synergistic combos and hoping for the artefacts to back them up. Also there are some set ups that are a LOT more difficult to progress than others - it should not be beyond the designers to make subtle changes to alter the "feel" of cards, but some just are so much weaker than others. The dice manipulation (needed to mitigate poor rolls) is a case in point, some of the spells are strong and flexible, while others are just meh...I have "Brute Forced" a win without much dice control, but it needed too much luck. The next thing that has made me stop is that the "quests" are getting silly in that you feel that you are getting sucked into sub-optimal play, or needing to "grind" to achieve them, I know this was early release but it's a long way from being polished and it isn't just tweaks like in the latest patch that are needed. I did spend just under 40 hours exploring the game so the money wasn't wasted, but as the the rewards get thinner the more you play, then this steeply "diminishing returns" just means I'm unlikely to come back to this ever.

Unlike many games in the dice roguelike genre, this one gives you the tools to manage the randomness that's thrown at you. Clever designs, a "build-your-own-run" difficulty system that makes you pick your own debuffs before higher level runs, and subclasses that change the way you approach your run all add up to a great experience. The game could use a few more bosses at each level for variety's sake, and sometimes it feels like it's too easy to break the game, even at higher difficulties. But at 35 hours in, I still feel like there's plenty of game worth playing. Well worth the price, and a steal if you ever catch it on sale.

As someone who has gotten all the achievements and "beaten" the game on the hardest difficulty levels... The dev's clearly have no idea about the direction they want to take this game and what makes it "fun". the last couple of big patches are mess of balance and strange choices. wait until full release...maybe then it will be worth it? *** Update for "full" release *** TLDR : if its on offer get it, if not don't bother until the devs learn what balancing is, which based on 3 or so years of patches...not likely Pros - Visually great - Fantastic Audio - Animations and "feel" is superb, although some super game play combos are still tedious and very time consuming - Creative ideas and uniqueness of all the different heros and abilities are right up there. - For the most part replayable Cons - Many extreamly "unfun" and "frustrating" mechanics in the game / enemies - Balancing all over the place - Final act 4 and "final" boss absolute snooze fest and the path to get there feels more like a punishment than an exciting adventure - Steep learning curve There are probably many more pros and cons but the jist is, an amazing concept and great ideas get ruined by poor game play loops and fake difficulty. Like alot of similar games (think slay the spire or monster train) it is possible with lots of luck to build really strong (and fun) builds that will always win regardless of mutator level. The issue is in Spellrogue alot of the builds are all or nothing when it comes to your RNG with getting what you need. You either will have it line up and you win, or you just dont get any and no matter how good you are are understanding the mechanics or making the "right" choice you just wont be able to scale well enough. And not just being lucky to get the right spells, its that alot of spells lack the ability to stand on their own. For example, lets take the new air hero. One of its gameplay concepts is ability "shifting". A really unique and thought provoking gameplay where you move your spells around on your cast bar and by doing so trigger different effects. However, for that build to be able to actually do damage and progress you require a rare spell or a sharded uncommon spell else you will be litterally taking 10-15 minutes per fight as you slowly wait for your passive lightning to make the kill. And while i'm not against having the strongest bits of these combos being rare, my issue is a build not working at all until you get said final bit. In the early days i felt that there was more means to an end then there are currently. Even if i did not get the perfect builds, i could still get over the finish line and be happy with it. Now i can already tell half way through the fist act if it will be worth it. THe other issue is that its clear that the devs have taken a very blanket approach to balancing and not understood how some mutators and debuffs when stacked against each other make the game unplayable. While hard to explain to someone who hasnt played the game, it seems that their creativity runs out when it comes to balancing and they throw in alot of really frustrating and sometimes impossible to deal with negative effects to "break" your builds. Again, i have no issue with encounters being differnet and forcing me to have a more rounded deck that isnt just a one trick, its just how they do it makes for some extreamey tediosu and boring gameplay. In continuation of balancing, don't even get me started on "shards". Shards are what you collect to upgrade your abilities and unlock additional spell slots. In the early version of the game the devs seemed to recognise that we want to get all of them and ultimately you could 9/10 collect enough shards to unlock all spells and have all your spells upgraded. Even at the highest mutators this was possible. And keep in mind that alot of the balancing of spells and their usefulness are hidden behind the shards. You will often find yourself only using a spell if you can upgrade it and the end game builds all require multiple spells to be upgraded. Then for whatever reason, about a year later the devs decided to drastically reduce the amount of shards you could get to the point that you maybe got 4 per run instead of the usual 9-11. So what then really boogles my mind is that they quickly reveresed this and it went back to a previous state but more ilke 7/10 now instead. So then why is it in the final release have they gone back and shards are a stupidly rare commodity that creates a frustrating experience. Final i just want to mention the "final" boss and act 4 which is just the most boring forced difficulty trek ive ever had to face and i will not bother doing it again. I'm going to compare this directly to slay the spire's act 4 when it first came out. Both artificially force you to go along certain paths to collect items to open the final portal, both then make you choose between that item and something useful. However it feels significantly more punishign and unfun in spellrogue than it does in slay the spire. When i was doing my attempt for the act 4 boss i restarted the map on the first load in numerous times because you need a path that leads you to the special event that ALSO allows you at fight at least one elite (ideally 2) and then hope that in act 2 and 3 dont get screwed by the pathing, This is RNG for paths with shards is a double whammy as you not only lack shards overall (see above) but then stupidly need to spend the precious shards breaking your own build to get to the final act. I got there with a dice destroying fire build that lost all of its "scaling" to get to the 4th act because i had to give up one of my shards just to access the damn thing. This mean that my build which should have taken about 10-14 turn to beat both each stage. ended up taking a stupid 40-45 turns because i was jsut waiting for passive damage to finish the job. So i can safely say that now ive done it got the achivement, thank you never agian. It just frustrates me so much to have devs that balance a game around reducing the "fun". The thing is i keep playing and coming back because the concept and ideas are good. and yet...all that creativity all those fun unique ideas disapear when it come to balancing and the mutators a real shame

To be honest, roguelikes (and -lights) are not my thing. I often find them too grindy and too "hardcore" to be actually enjoyable. I bounced off Slay the Spire hard, mostly due to its difficulty and the bazillion cards you meed to find in order to succeed. But I gave Spellrogue a try after they've won the GOTY award, and it's actually quite enjoyable. A run is short, and I was even able to win a few. The spell dice mechanic is very addictive, and the deck crafting complex enough (but not too complex) to understand the different approaches with each character. Like most these games I played, the focus seems to be hard on the game mechanics, so don't expect a narrative à la darkest dungeon here. The production value is good for an indy game, and I really appreciated that I didn't need to look at yet another pixel art game. There might be more flashy games out there, but let's not expect insane things from a three man team. tldr; it's a fun roguelike game for a casual player like me

As you can see from my hours played, I've spent a lot of time on this game. It was really fun. It found that nice niche area where you could play repeatedly, and there was enough randomness and variation that it wasn't always the same, and yet you weren't wholly reliant on getting lucky draws on the spells etc. offered. Then they brought out a new update. I know downvoting a game based on the latest update is a tale as old as video games (or, like, at least five years or something), but this update pisses me off. Firstly, I was in the middle of a run that I was enjoying. I log in to find out that with the update, my run has been lost. Secondly, and far more egregious: Some enemies have the ability to put spell reflect on one of their allies. This meant you have to kill this enemy in order to remove this protection and kill the protected ally. Fair enough. But with the latest update, the spell reflection effect persists between turns... and even after the creature that applied it is dead. So I'm 70% of the way through a run with the newly-introduced storm character, when I stumble on this set of enemies, duly dispatch the other two, and then find myself face to face with the last enemy, who is protected by spell reflection. Leaving me no choice but to kill myself. How the hell did this crap make it through play-testing? Awful decision. I hope it will be quickly rectified in a scramble to fix this f**k-up. But it's already pissed me off and lowered my opinion of this game. Another complaint I have is that the method for prolonging the game by extending the difficulty is also badly done. Rather than give you the option of straightforwardly engaging in runs against more difficult opponents, they try to make things more interesting by giving options to hobble your own abilities. This was a bad idea when it was first thought of in some other game many years ago, and it remains a bad idea now. The basic game mechanics of this game are very well done. It's a good premise, well-executed. I'm pretty picky about these things, and it's rare that I come back to a game as often as I have to this one. Please sort your crap out so I can keep playing.

纯故意折磨玩家的坐牢游戏，数值完全不平衡，小怪跟精英怪似的。

数值平衡到后面实在太烂了，怪物第二章开始伤害稳定两位数，而角色的遗物都是个位数加成，骰子打个boss才给加一个，如果不糊一回合技能都用不了几个，伤害对比怪物天差地别。 最重要的是制作组还给你隐晦的加了时间限制，随处可见的怪物增益，这怪加属性比我还勤奋。点名批评粪中粪第三层的法术枯萎，本来角色技能组都要靠启动，你还给他回合数增加禁封技能，伤害还贼高，完全不懂制作组的脑回路怎么想的。这种打法无论什么套路，只要你敢拖就百分百打不过，最终boss都比他简单，极大地限制了套路搭配。 最幽默的就是火哥，真是要笑死了，火的主要套路是碎骰子，但是偏偏里面又加了大量的高数值技能，骰子又有数量限制，前期没抽到关键技能基本gg，杂耍一套对面怪物说还好我技高一筹。更别说他的蓝卡居然绝大多数都是不可再生的，拜托后面怪物打下三四十点，你给个回血的+4+6居然只敢给玩家用三四次，用它我都亏资源，搞笑呢。回血给的这么吝啬，但是火的卖血卡给的又这么多，但这买血给的+2+3的，他配和其他几个角色的机制比吗？

先说优点：作为骰子肉鸽，可玩性是同类游戏里比较不错的。丰富的骰池搭配技能、符文、遗物，让玩家每一把都有不同的体验；四职业每个都做了几套不同的初始卡组和遗物，有明显的区分度；局外解锁也够玩很久。 目前最大的问题是难度，牢点诸多： 一、对比尖塔，每一层的长度短了很多，导致发育非常受限，看不了几组牌就要见boss。改善方法要么额外花金币多刷一组牌，要么火堆看牌，前者影响购物后者影响回复； 二、进阶难度非常坐牢，每层选一个限制器，这种不知道是哪个小可爱设计的，建议自己玩一下。有些真要敢选分分钟对面就是红石三鸟、血量乐嘉，高级的限制器个个要命避无可避。而且是每层选一个！！！每层！！ 三、真结局，条件繁琐，锁路线严重，发育倒扣，打到第四层的只有0.8%。 1.0版本目前不打算继续坐牢了。什么时候限制器改了，玩家发育加强了，再考虑改评测
用火人过了堕落13，总体感觉还不错的肉鸽卡牌游戏。四个角色特点鲜明也具有不同构筑方向所以bd还算丰富。缺点是堕落的很多限制器在高难度非常逆天，基本上得反复roll开局才能打过高难度堕落，希望后续版本能改进。

游戏其实挺好玩的，低难度下我都是一把过的，可以尝试各种套路通关，而一到高难度就非常难受，水人我打了10几次才过了动荡13打了隐藏boss。 游戏在平衡上问题非常大。首先是变异，绝大多数变异根本就没法拿，负面效果太大了，拿了要么前期暴毙，要么开局就知道不可能打过隐藏boss。其次是卡牌，设计太过于保守，数值很低，搭配着变异给怪增强根本就打不过，特别是力量，一个骰子就加个几点，一点用都没有，而反观激怒，随便都可以叠到20层以上，配合多段一下就把怪全杀了。最后就是怪物，几乎所有怪物设计的都是有成长性的，而且成长非常猛，第一层就有一个每回合加3力的怪，就逼着你快速击杀，前期拿不到高伤的法术就会大掉血。 学学杀戮尖塔，虽然进阶20一样很难，但是通过sl总有一个事件线是可以通关的，无解的种子目前只有2个，而你这个游戏的动荡13，绝大多数局就不可能通关，你设计师自己去试试。 什么时候高难度能玩了，我再来改好评。

Short version: If you're good with a short game and just a little replay value, I can recommend. If you want to experience all the content and master any of the higher difficulties, it's a horrible chore. While it has a charming and easy start, and is fun for a bit, and while the middle of the game is a fun challenge, the late game suffers from serious grind and is just a horrific slog. There are 13 levels of difficulty, but the game stops being fun around the 6th level, because it imposes semi-random and very onerous effects that suck the fun out. Some runs will be going swimmingly until you're forced to choose a debuff that hard-counters your build, or between ones that cripple your ability to really play at all. Likewise, if you have a build, there's an enemy that will hard counter it, so you have to simply hope that you don't randomly encounter such an enemy. Bosses are typically far easier than the regular elite monsters, which seem specifically designed to defeat all but a tiny fraction of builds and play styles. This makes it really hard to choose things that are fun or play with builds and combinations, because you can't afford any experimentation or deviation. And playing with the builds should be the most fun part of the game. After that, the game operates by attracting addiction-prone personalities to the slot-machine like build make-or-break RNG effects. But I guess I'm a filthy casual and don't have patience for that. Or the dopamine treadmill just isn't working on me. But up to that point, I really enjoyed the game. So if you're OK with getting maybe 15-20 hours out of it before it becomes a chore, this game may actually be a great fit for you, and you should try it. You'll know within 2 hours if it's going to be fun for a bit. But it's hard to imagine the level of obsessive dedication it would require to actually complete the content. Disclaimer: My play time is highly inflated by leaving it running over a weekend. I would say I sit at about 40-50% completion.

The game Slay the Spire should have been. Spellrogue does things so much better. You feel like you can actually make choices on your runs instead of being at the mercy of the RNG. Do you get screwed by the dice some turns? Yes. Can you almost always play smart and get out of it. Yes again. Having so many options during a run practically guarantees that you will run into cards that synergies with your current deck. In my first 10 hours I did not have any runs that would have ended on a single instance of bad luck or mistake I made. For this price it is a steal. After some meta progression you get to tailor your run experience to your liking in a way I hope more games did. Two down sides I have to bring up. Some of the artifacts are just bad or bland or both. Some of the keywords have very ambiguous explanations in card view. That is not good when you are deciding if you should spend resources on them. For example since all conditions have several levels, they should tell in the description what additional levels do.

Have tested this game for a quite a few runs (maybe 16 hours? Fell asleep with computer on) - and while it initially was a breath of fresh air and dices are a new mechanic... Well what you do with them, given your spells, becomes very repetitive. And while I agree Slay the Spire also can be repetitive this differs by requiring much more effort to roll dice and put them in the correct place. As well as generally fights having a much slower pace and lacks "fun" combos (there is the rain option and some possible things to try out, but creativity seems limited). I feel one does way less damage, constantly have to balance attack and shields, and grind yourself through every enemy... which after a while becomes more a chore than fun. I tried giving this a shot but ends up being a thumbs down.

This is a very solid roguelike deckbuilder for the price. I got it for $10 (50% off), but I would have been happy with it even at full price. There are a lot of mechanics to learn between all the different status effects, dice enchantments, buffs and debuffs, etc. that each run will feel like a new challenge, yet it's still not excessively complicated. All the cards have very concise descriptions using pictograms which make them quick and easy to read. I also like that you can recover and repurpose your shards (card upgrade resource) without penalty so you don't get locked in to anything. I really like the art style and the character/monster designs and animations as well. All that said, it's not a perfect game. There are some cards and deck strategies that seem too difficult to play that I haven't even tried, like burning spell charges or Sefyra's card re-org stuff. Battles can take a really long time when you roll a ton of dice, then use your dice manipulation spells, then you assign the dice to your attacks and defense which sometimes also give you more dice. There's even an achievement for rolling 50 dice in a turn, but that's also 50 dice you have to individually play too. Should elite and boss battles sometimes take 15+ minutes? It's not every run at least, sometimes you can make a build that crushes everything quickly. Still well worth it for $10. I think it's better than Slay the Spire.

Spellrogue is a dice-based roguelike with tactical combat and fresh mechanics. The variety of heroes, spells, and strategies keeps it entertaining through every run. A must-play for roguelike fans!
SpellRogue’s unique mechanic of re-rolling and manipulating dice takes the genre to a whole new level.
SpellRogue is a dark fantasy roguelike deckbuilder built on dice. Each turn you roll a pool of mana dice and spend them to power your spells, manipulating the rolls to turn chance into strategy.
